The US Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, US time, after a communications problem affected air traffic control centres, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said. The stop lasted more than four hours before departures resumed, according to AAP and the ABC.

The ABC reported more than 11,000 flights were delayed or cancelled and about 600 diverted. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said early findings pointed to a telecommunications failure, with no sign of an attack so far. Duffy said US$30 billion is needed to upgrade air traffic control. Australian travel industry representatives said travellers due to fly within 72 hours were being prioritised.
keyFacts: Ground stop lasted more than four hours
ABC reports 11,000+ flights delayed or cancelled
Officials say no sign of an attack so far

articles.title: Australia and Philippines to sign defence cooperation agreement in Manila
articles.summary:
Australia and the Philippines are expected to sign a defence cooperation agreement on Sunday on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit in Manila, the ABC and SBS reported. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese arrived in Manila on Saturday from the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye.

According to the ABC, the deal is expected to expand reciprocal military access and information sharing and support the Philippine navy and coastguard. SBS reported it would cover maritime awareness and interoperability. China's foreign ministry has told Australia to stop inciting confrontation, the ABC said. Albanese may meet US President Donald Trump, who is due at ASEAN on 17 November, AAP reported.
keyFacts: Signing expected Sunday in Manila
Covers military access and information sharing
Trump due at ASEAN on 17 November

articles.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said two oil tankers exploded and caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a statement on Iranian state television reported by ANI and Aaj News. It said one was a supertanker and that both had switched off radar and positioning systems to cross by an unauthorised route.

Iran did not name the ships or their flags, and the claims have not been independently confirmed. The US military has said it has cleared the main shipping lanes of mines. Al Jazeera described it as the third reported tanker incident in about 24 hours.
keyFacts: Ships and flags were not named
Claims not independently confirmed
US says main lanes cleared of mines

articles.title: ICC judges close part of Afghanistan probe that covered alleged US troop crimes
articles.summary:
Judges at the International Criminal Court have closed the part of the prosecutor's Afghanistan investigation that could examine alleged crimes by US forces, along with a probe into the Islamic State affiliate ISIS-K, according to Reuters and AP reports carried by Al Jazeera and Defense News. The investigation will now focus on the Taliban's conduct since 2021.

The judges cited significant limits on the prosecution's ability to investigate. The prosecutor's office said it had appealed. The US is not an ICC member and has sanctioned court staff. Arrest warrants for four Taliban leaders remain in force, Reuters reported.
keyFacts: Focus narrowed to Taliban conduct since 2021
Prosecutor's office has appealed
Warrants for four Taliban leaders remain

articles.title: Türkiye and Qatar sign mutual defence agreement
articles.summary:
Türkiye and Qatar have signed a mutual defence agreement committing them to a unified position against any external armed attack on either country, according to AFP and Al Jazeera. It was signed after President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan met Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani in Istanbul on Friday.

A joint statement carried by Qatar's state news agency said the pact covers consultation on threats, joint exercises, defence industry cooperation and training, AFP reported. Erdoğan's office said it added a new dimension to ties, and the emir called it a strategic partnership. Other agreements signed included one on conflict resolution.
keyFacts: Signed in Istanbul on Friday
Pledges joint stance against external attack
Covers exercises, industry and training

articles.title: US gives states six more months before enforcing Medicaid work requirements
articles.summary:
The Trump administration said on Friday, US time, that states will have six more months before they must enforce new Medicaid work requirements, moving enforcement to 1 July 2027, STAT reported. States had been preparing to start on 1 January.

The rules, from last year's budget law, require many working-age adults covered under Medicaid expansion to work, study or volunteer 80 hours a month unless exempt. STAT reported that states had sued the federal health agency CMS seeking a delay until exemptions for medically frail people were settled, and that a judge recently rejected the administration's definition of medical frailty.
keyFacts: Enforcement moved to 1 July 2027
Requirement is 80 hours a month
States had sued seeking a delay

articles.title: New York Fed report confirms US Treasury bought yen in July
articles.summary:
The US Treasury bought Japanese yen in the July–September quarter while the Federal Reserve made no foreign exchange interventions of its own, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York said in its quarterly report. Reuters reported the New York Fed bought 79.4 billion yen for the Treasury on 31 July, paid for with euros from the Exchange Stabilization Fund.

Japan's Finance Ministry spent 15.4 trillion yen on intervention in the same quarter, according to Reuters. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in August the US would not hesitate to join further action. The yen has since weakened back towards 160 per US dollar, Reuters said.
keyFacts: 79.4 billion yen bought on 31 July
Fed made no interventions of its own
Japan spent 15.4 trillion yen in the quarter

articles.title: Houthis say they fired missiles at Saudi forces in Jazan
articles.summary:
Yemen's Houthis said on Friday they fired two ballistic missiles at Saudi forces at Al-Tuwal in Jazan province, Reuters reported. The claim came hours after Saudi civil defence declared an all-clear in the province, and Reuters said it was unclear if the two were linked. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation.

The Houthis also claimed attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and on a pumping station on the East-West oil pipeline, according to Reuters. Saudi Arabia has been rerouting about 4 million barrels of oil a day through that pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu.
keyFacts: Houthis claim two ballistic missiles fired
No immediate Saudi confirmation
Airport and pipeline attacks also claimed

articles.title: India targets 900 gigawatts of clean power by 2035 as coal use continues
articles.summary:
India has set a goal of 900 gigawatts of non-fossil power capacity by 2035, almost double its 500-gigawatt target for 2030, AP reported. Its current clean capacity is just over 300 gigawatts, third behind China and the US.

A University of California, Berkeley researcher told AP the target cannot be met unless the grid is upgraded. The government has approved nearly US$20 billion for grid and storage projects. Coal produced about 71 per cent of India's electricity in 2025, according to the think tank Ember, and the head of India's Central Electricity Authority said up to 150 gigawatts of new coal may be needed by 2035.
keyFacts: Target nearly doubles 2030 goal
Current clean capacity just over 300GW
Coal supplied about 71% of 2025 power

articles.title: Victorian Labor pledges $1.17 billion for school upgrades if re-elected
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor would spend more than $1.17 billion upgrading 228 public schools if re-elected, Premier Ben Carroll said on Saturday, AAP reported. The package includes $500 million for non-government schools, made up of $350 million for Catholic schools and $150 million for low-fee independent schools.

Education Minister Gabrielle Williams asked Opposition Leader Jess Wilson which upgrades she would cut. Wilson has alleged the government made secret cuts to non-government school funding, which Labor denies, saying it was keeping funding within national entitlements. Wilson described the pledge as another large pre-election promise, according to AAP.
keyFacts: 228 public schools to be upgraded
$500m for non-government schools
Opposition alleges funding cuts; Labor denies

articles.title: ProPublica reports Georgia election board members worked with Cleta Mitchell network
articles.summary:
Current and former members of Georgia's State Election Board coordinated with lawyer Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network and allied groups, ProPublica reported, citing recordings of private calls and events. It reported that the board's executive director, James Mills, worked closely with network members, according to five sources.

Board chair John Fervier told ProPublica the network's influence should stop. Vice chair Janelle King said activists did not influence her decisions, and Mills declined to answer questions. Mitchell praised the network's work with the board, and network figure Garland Favorito called the report's central claim a false conspiracy theory.
keyFacts: Based on recordings of private calls
Board chair says influence should stop
Network figure calls claim false

articles.title: Zelenskiy says US raised idea of Ukraine leaving Donbas in exchange for NATO entry
articles.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said US negotiators asked whether Kyiv would pull its forces out of the Donbas region if Ukraine were admitted to NATO, according to Reuters and AAP. He said it was the first time membership had been tied to territorial concessions in the talks.

Zelenskiy said Ukraine was not ready to give up territory, but would put such a question to a referendum if it received a full package of security guarantees, military support and reconstruction funding. He also said Russian President Vladimir Putin did not personally support a ceasefire. Moscow's response to the idea was not reported.
keyFacts: Two days of US-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended without a major breakthrough
The sides agreed a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people, Reuters reported
EU leaders named Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and EU officials as Europe's negotiating team

articles.title: US loses measles elimination status after 26 years
articles.summary:
The United States no longer qualifies as having eliminated measles, according to a decision by an expert commission reporting to the Pan American Health Organization, CBS News and CNN reported on Friday US time. The Wall Street Journal first reported the finding. The US had held the status since 2000.

CBS said the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has counted 5,412 cases in 2026, the most since 1991, and at least six deaths, while state health departments have reported 10 deaths, according to Al Jazeera. The CDC says 96 per cent of this year's infections were in people who were unvaccinated or whose status was unknown. PAHO is due to hold a news conference on Tuesday.
keyFacts: Status is lost when one chain of transmission continues for more than 12 months
Cases have been confirmed in 45 states and Washington DC, CBS said
Kindergarten vaccination fell from 95.2 to 92.4 per cent between 2019-20 and 2025-26, Al Jazeera reported

articles.title: US flight disruption continues; Duffy says contractor router flooded FAA network
articles.summary:
US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router installed during work by contractor L3Harris at a remote Federal Aviation Administration site began flooding other routers in the air traffic control network, causing Friday's nationwide ground stop, according to Yahoo News. He said officials were still determining whether the cause was contractor error or faulty equipment, and that it was not a cyber attack.

FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said 4,000 to 5,000 of about 41,000 scheduled flights would be cancelled on Saturday, with schedules expected to return to normal by the end of Sunday. New York Governor Kathy Hochul called for Duffy to resign. L3Harris's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Flightradar24 counted nearly 10,000 cancellations from the stoppage, ABC reported
Bedford said the ground stop was the longest since 11 September 2001
Airlines will not have to compensate passengers because the fault was in FAA systems, ABC said

articles.title: UN says at least 25 seafarers killed around Strait of Hormuz since February
articles.summary:
At least 25 seafarers have been killed in and around the Strait of Hormuz since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, UN Assistant Secretary-General Khaled Khiari told the Security Council on Friday, according to Al Jazeera. He said the situation should not be allowed to become normal.

The International Maritime Organization recorded 136 security incidents involving ships between 1 March and 11 November, including 35 in October and 10 so far in November, Khiari said. Iranian authorities said on Saturday that three oil tankers had hit mines in restricted areas, while the US military says the main shipping routes have been cleared.
keyFacts: Figures cover the period up to 11 November
Shipping through the strait is about 65 per cent below pre-war levels, according to UKMTO
Iran and the US give conflicting accounts of whether the routes are safe

articles.title: Hungary recovers nearly $US20 million in cash in probe of Orbán-era minister
articles.summary:
Hungarian authorities have recovered almost $US20 million in cash in a bribery investigation into Miklós Seszták, a development minister under former prime minister Viktor Orbán, Reuters reported. Some of the money was buried in forests and some hidden in farm buildings and warehouses, according to the report. Seszták denies wrongdoing.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar, who replaced Orbán after April's election, described the find as the end of a Fidesz "mafia". Fidesz's response was not included in the Reuters report. Two former ministers and former central bank governor György Matolcsy are under arrest in separate cases and deny wrongdoing.
keyFacts: Recovered sums were 5.07 billion forints, €2.66 million and $US1.26 million
Orbán governed for 16 years before losing power in April
A Median survey puts Fidesz support at 16 per cent, Reuters said

articles.title: COP31: UN climate chief urges faster progress as ministers arrive in Antalya
articles.summary:
UN climate chief Simon Stiell described progress at the COP31 talks in Antalya as constructive on Saturday and urged governments to move quickly to the hardest issues, according to Climate Home News and Reuters. A stocktaking plenary chaired by Türkiye and Australia was scheduled for Saturday night as ministers arrived for the final week.

At least 15 countries have backed a voluntary pledge to lift electricity's share of global final energy use to 35 per cent by 2035, from 23 per cent now, Climate Home reported. African nations are seeking adaptation finance of at least $US120 billion a year by 2035. Civil society groups criticised a draft note on a just transition mechanism, which Chris Bowen called comprehensive.
keyFacts: Australia's Chris Bowen is president of negotiations
EU negotiator Wopke Hoekstra signalled the EU may drop the word 'clean' from electrification wording
Brazil's President Lula said Brazil should host the next fossil fuel phase-out conference

articles.title: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins elected Alaska governor
articles.summary:
Former state legislator Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins has been elected governor of Alaska, the first Democrat to win the office since 1998, according to CBS News and the Associated Press. He defeated three Republican candidates, including one endorsed by President Donald Trump, after more than a week of counting.

Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, said the state had been poorly served under outgoing Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy, citing ferry service cuts, and pledged a cabinet drawing on Republicans, Democrats and independents. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski endorsed him a week before polling day. Responses from his Republican opponents were not included in the CBS report.
keyFacts: Alaska voted on 3 November
Democrats will hold 30 governorships after the midterms, CBS said
Three former Alaska governors backed Kreiss-Tomkins

articles.title: Alaska voters reject repeal of ranked-choice voting and open primaries
articles.summary:
A ballot measure to repeal Alaska's open top-four primaries and ranked-choice general elections has failed, according to an Associated Press call reported by NPR. It is the second time voters have rejected a repeal, after a 2024 measure failed by 743 votes, Alaska Public Media reported.

Supporters of repeal argued the system is confusing, while opponents of repeal said it gives voters more choice, according to Alaska Public Media. The campaign against repeal raised about $10.4 million, compared with about $2.6 million for the repeal side, the outlet reported. Nick Troiano of Unite America said Alaskans had spoken.
keyFacts: The measure was Ballot Measure 2 at the 3 November election
Elon Musk gave $1.5 million to a group backing repeal, Alaska Public Media said
The US Senate race has two candidates named Dan Sullivan and may go to ranked tabulation, NPR said

articles.title: Report card finds Australia making no progress on reducing rabbit numbers
articles.summary:
Australia's rabbit numbers, spread and impacts have remained largely unchanged over five years, according to the government-compiled Vertebrate Pest Management Report Card, AAP reported. Populations have increased in Victoria, Tasmania and the ACT, and environmental damage is worsening in NSW and Tasmania.

Experts estimate there are about 200 million rabbits nationally, threatening 322 listed species and causing more than $200 million a year in farm losses, AAP said. The federal Established Pest Animals and Weeds program had no ongoing funding in the last budget, with a decision due next year. Reece Pianta of the Invasive Species Council said funding cuts were allowing populations to spread. A government response was not reported.
keyFacts: Rabbits are becoming resistant to the haemorrhagic disease virus released almost a decade ago
The government funded $2.6 million for new biocontrol research this year
Rabbits were released in Victoria in 1859

articles.title: Health leaders back 2040 goal to end rheumatic heart disease as Australia faces criticism
articles.summary:
Global health leaders have backed a Perth Declaration aiming to eliminate rheumatic heart disease and acute rheumatic fever by 2040, the ABC reported. Experts said Australia appears willing to tolerate some of the world's highest rates of the disease, mainly among First Nations people.

About 12,000 people in Australia live with the disease or have a history of rheumatic fever, and First Nations people make up four in five cases, according to the ABC. World Heart Federation president Jagat Narula said Australia had committed only a small part of the $689 million needed for its national strategy. The federal government said it is investing $95.8 million, and Assistant Minister Rebecca White pointed to housing and sanitation work.
keyFacts: First Nations people die from the disease at more than five times the non-Indigenous rate
Australia's national Endgame Strategy targets 2031
Acute rheumatic fever can be treated with penicillin, a Heart Foundation adviser said

articles.title: Australia and the Philippines sign updated defence cooperation agreement
articles.summary:
Australia and the Philippines have signed a defence cooperation agreement in Manila during Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's visit, according to the Manila Times and Rappler. The deal updates a defence arrangement between the two countries that dates from 1995.

Rappler and other outlets reported the updated agreement is meant to speed up coordination between the two militaries, including for disaster response. Bloomberg, via the Japan Times, reported the upgrade comes as both countries focus on China's activity in the region. Mr Albanese travels on to the ASEAN summit, where US President Donald Trump is due to attend, AAP reported. Beijing's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
keyFacts: The agreement updates a 1995 defence arrangement
It was signed in Manila on 15 November
The signing was flagged by both governments on 14 November

articles.title: Iran's navy says three oil tankers hit mines in Hormuz and are on fire
articles.summary:
Iran's navy has said three oil tankers struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, according to Arab News, Middle East Eye and the Manila Times. A day earlier, Iran's Revolutionary Guards had said two oil tankers hit mines in the strait.

The vessels' names, flags and any casualties were not independently confirmed in the reports reviewed. The incidents follow a series of attacks and explosions involving ships in and near the strait in recent days, which Iran has linked to ships ignoring its warnings. The United Nations said on Saturday at least 25 seafarers had been killed around the strait since February.

Iran says the ships caught fire
The claims have not been independently verified

articles.title: Israeli air strike kills senior Hamas commander in southern Gaza
articles.summary:
An Israeli air strike has killed a senior commander in Hamas's armed wing in southern Gaza, Al Jazeera reported. The Israeli military said it targeted a senior member of the group's military wing, according to Arab News and the Times of Israel.

Indian and regional outlets reported that Hamas confirmed the death of a Rafah-area commander, though the identity was not confirmed across the sources reviewed. The strike follows other Israeli strikes in Gaza this week, including one on Nasser Hospital that the Gaza health ministry said killed six people. Israel's military says it targets militants. Casualty figures from Sunday's strike were not confirmed in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: The strike was in southern Gaza
Israel's military says it targeted a senior Hamas military figure
It follows deadly strikes earlier in the week

articles.title: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition has said it intercepted two missiles and two drones over Riyadh, according to Al Jazeera. Arab News and Pakistan's Express Tribune reported the coalition also said it brought down drones over the kingdom's Eastern Province.

The coalition attributed the attacks to Yemen's Houthi movement, Arab News reported. Damage or casualties were not reported in the sources reviewed. The Houthis said on Saturday they had fired missiles at Saudi forces in Jazan, as fighting between the two sides has intensified over the past week. Al Jazeera's live coverage reported further drone interceptions later in the day.
keyFacts: Two missiles and two drones were intercepted over Riyadh, the coalition says
Drones were also downed over the Eastern Province
The coalition blames the Houthis

articles.title: Iraq's prime minister sacks nine officials over alleged oil smuggling
articles.summary:
Iraq's prime minister has dismissed nine officials over alleged oil smuggling in an area regarded as a stronghold of pro-Iran armed groups, according to Al Jazeera, The New Arab and Arab News.

Al Jazeera reported the probe concerns smuggling worth about $US30 million. Al Jazeera described the area as a stronghold of a powerful militia. The officials' names and the specific allegations against them were not detailed in the sources reviewed, and responses from the dismissed officials or the armed groups were not reported. The dismissals were announced on Saturday, local time, according to the reports.
keyFacts: Nine officials were dismissed
The alleged smuggling was in a pro-Iran group stronghold
Al Jazeera put the smuggling at about $US30 million

articles.title: Victorian Labor makes $1 billion surgery plan centrepiece of campaign launch
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor has made a plan to spend about $1 billion on surgery the main announcement of its state election campaign launch, AAP reported. Premier Jacinta Allan presented the pledge at the party's launch in Melbourne on Sunday, according to AAP and the ABC.

The ABC reported both major parties held launches on the same day, with Labor focused on health and the Coalition on youth crime. Deputy Premier Ben Carroll also addressed the Labor launch, according to reports. Full costings and timelines for the surgery plan were not detailed in the reports reviewed, and the Coalition's response to the pledge was not reported. Victorians vote on 28 November, and Labor has governed the state since 2014.

Both major parties launched their campaigns on 15 November

articles.title: Victorian Coalition pledges regional bootcamp prison for young offenders
articles.summary:
Victorian Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has announced a Coalition plan for a regional bootcamp-style prison for young offenders, the ABC reported. The facility would be at Dhurringile in northern Victoria, according to the ABC, and the plan was unveiled at the Coalition's campaign launch on Sunday.

AAP reported the bootcamp was a central announcement of the Liberal launch. Ms Wilson said she was taking nothing for granted, according to reports of the launch. Details of cost, capacity and opening date were not set out in the reports reviewed, and Labor's response to the plan was not reported. Victorians vote on 28 November.
keyFacts: The site proposed is Dhurringile
The plan targets young offenders
It was announced at the Coalition's campaign launch

articles.title: SpaceX catches Starship upper stage at launch tower for the first time
articles.summary:
SpaceX has caught the Starship spacecraft with its launch tower's mechanical arms after a flight around Earth, the first time it has recovered the vehicle's upper stage this way, according to Al Jazeera, the ABC and Space.com. The 15th Starship test flight launched from Starbase in Texas.

The Statesman and other outlets reported the ship completed about 14 orbits before returning. SpaceX has previously caught the Super Heavy booster with the tower, but earlier upper stages splashed down or were lost. The company says catching both stages is key to making the rocket fully reusable, which NASA is relying on for its planned crewed Moon landings.
