SpaceX had previously caught only the booster

articles.title: Netanyahu calls for unity government with Eisenkot, citing Iran threat
articles.summary:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has urged opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot to negotiate a national unity government, saying only a broad coalition could deal with Iran's nuclear threat, according to Xinhua and JNS. JNS reported he called for talks without preconditions.

Israel's new parliament was sworn in last week with no bloc holding a majority. Mr Eisenkot has said Likud must break with far-right partners and accept his principles before joining any government, Ynet reported. Mr Netanyahu's coalition partners and opposition parties have both objected to the unity proposal, according to i24 News. No agreement has been announced.
keyFacts: Netanyahu called for unity talks without preconditions
He cited the threat from Iran's nuclear program
No bloc holds a Knesset majority

articles.title: Home auction clearance rates fall to fresh low, AAP reports
articles.summary:
Home auction clearance rates fell to a fresh low at the weekend as fewer buyers bid, AAP reported on Sunday. The report was based on preliminary results, which showed a smaller share of homes offered at auction selling than in previous weeks.

Final results are usually higher than preliminary figures once late reports are counted. The weaker results follow ABS data last week showing new home loan commitments fell 15 per cent in the September quarter, the largest drop on record. MacroBusiness also reported the auction market had reached a new low this month.
keyFacts: AAP says clearance rates hit a fresh low
Figures are preliminary
New home lending fell 15 per cent in the September quarter, the ABS said

articles.title: Bahrain says it intercepted Iranian drones; Iran claims hit on US radar at Riffa base
articles.summary:
Bahrain's military said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks early on Sunday, after sirens and explosions were reported across the kingdom. Bahrain's Foreign Ministry said it held Iran fully responsible.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they launched six drones at a US air defence radar at the Riffa base, according to Iranian media cited by Al Jazeera. Neither US nor Bahraini authorities confirmed any radar was hit. The US military had denied an Iranian claim on Friday that a radar in Bahrain was destroyed. Iran's parliamentary speaker told Al Jazeera that Tehran had sent seven conditions for a deal through a Qatari mediator and was awaiting a US reply.
keyFacts: Bahrain says it intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks on Sunday
IRGC says it sent six drones at a US radar at Riffa
No confirmation from the US or Bahrain that the radar was hit

articles.title: Trump asks Congress to fund new air traffic control network as US cancellations continue
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump on Sunday called on Congress to fund a new air traffic control system, two days after a communications failure forced a nationwide ground stop, UPI reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on NBC's Meet the Press that he wants to move the network away from contractor L3Harris, according to UPI.

The White House said the failure came from overloaded 1980s-era equipment and that there was no evidence of a cyber attack. It said Mr Duffy has asked Congress for $US50 billion in emergency funding. Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen said Congress had already met the administration's request. About 6,700 flights were cancelled on Saturday, and more than 1,800 by midday Sunday, UPI reported, citing FlightAware.
keyFacts: Trump urged Congress to pay for a new air traffic control network
Duffy has sought $US50 billion in emergency funding, the White House says
More than 1,800 US flights were cancelled by midday Sunday, per FlightAware

articles.title: ASEAN leaders open annual summit in Manila; Trump due to arrive on Tuesday
articles.summary:
Southeast Asian leaders opened their annual summit in Manila on Sunday for three days of talks, with conflicts led by the Middle East war expected to top the agenda, according to AP, which cited draft communiqués. US President Donald Trump is due to arrive on Tuesday near the summit's close.

AFP reported Mr Trump is expected to join a Quad meeting with India, Japan and Australia on the sidelines. Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro said talks on a South China Sea code of conduct were "80 per cent" complete, though a regional diplomat told AFP no signing was expected. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr will hand the rotating chair to Singapore.
keyFacts: Summit opened in Manila on Sunday and runs three days
Trump expected Tuesday, with a Quad meeting planned, AFP says
Philippines says South China Sea code talks are 80 per cent done

articles.title: Albanese raises detained Melbourne activist Tran Hiep with Vietnam's prime minister
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese raised consular cases, including that of detained Australian Tran Hiep, with Vietnamese Prime Minister Le Minh Hung at the ASEAN summit in Manila on Sunday, AAP reported, citing an Australian readout.

Mr Hiep, a Melbourne democracy activist, has been held in Vietnam since he went missing in Cambodia in September. Vietnam's Ministry of Public Security said he and a Norwegian citizen were detained after allegedly trying to cross the border illegally and had admitted belonging to Viet Tan, which Vietnam lists as a terrorist group. Viet Tan says the men were abducted in Cambodia. The leaders also discussed trade, which reached a record $30 billion in 2025, AAP reported.
keyFacts: Albanese raised Tran Hiep's case with Vietnam's PM on Sunday
Vietnam says Hiep tried to cross illegally; Viet Tan says he was abducted
Two-way trade reached a record $30 billion in 2025

articles.title: Jordan court sentences three men to death over Karak church attack
articles.summary:
Jordan's State Security Court on Sunday sentenced three men to death by hanging over the 23 October gun attack on St George's Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate, according to the military and state news agency Petra.

Nine people were killed during a funeral service. Al Jazeera reported 25 people were wounded, while The National put the figure at 34. Authorities said the men, two brothers and a relative by marriage, were arrested three days after the attack following a clash with security forces. They were convicted of terrorist acts causing death, weapons offences and conspiracy, and one of financing terrorism. The National reported the ruling can be appealed and is automatically reviewed.
keyFacts: Three men sentenced to death by Jordan's State Security Court
Nine people were killed in the 23 October attack
The ruling can be appealed and is automatically reviewed, The National says

articles.title: Some Republican senators resist Trump judicial picks before Democrats take Senate
articles.summary:
Some Republican senators have blocked or questioned three of President Donald Trump's judicial nominees from their home states as he seeks to fill seats before Democrats take control of the Senate, Reuters reported. The Senate has confirmed 57 of his second-term judicial nominees.

The White House withdrew Judge Lee Rudofsky's nomination to the 8th Circuit after Arkansas senators John Boozman and Tom Cotton opposed it, and named state Supreme Court Justice Cody Hiland instead, Reuters said. Retiring Republican Thom Tillis said senators deserved more respect in the selection process. Majority Leader John Thune said confirmations were a top priority, with 23 nominees pending. A White House official said it expects all to be confirmed this year.
keyFacts: 57 Trump judicial nominees confirmed in his second term, Reuters says
Rudofsky's 8th Circuit nomination withdrawn after home-state opposition
23 nominees pending; White House expects all confirmed this year

articles.title: US attorney tells Senator Warren to preserve records over planned probes of Trump allies
articles.summary:
Aaron Reitz, the US Attorney for the Southern District of Texas, sent Democratic senator Elizabeth Warren a letter on Sunday demanding she preserve records linked to planned congressional investigations of people and companies associated with President Donald Trump, Newsweek and Anadolu reported.

The letter cites federal civil rights conspiracy laws and argues such inquiries lack a legitimate legislative purpose, according to Anadolu. Mr Reitz pointed to a television interview in which Ms Warren said she planned to investigate technology and Wall Street executives. He sent similar notices earlier to senators Richard Blumenthal and Elissa Slotkin; Mr Blumenthal called the implied threat baseless. Ms Warren had not responded publicly. Newsweek noted a preservation demand is not a subpoena.
keyFacts: Letter sent Sunday by the US Attorney for southern Texas
Warren given until 23 November to confirm compliance
Similar notices went to senators Blumenthal and Slotkin

articles.title: Illicit tobacco market shrinks for first time in five years, commission data show
articles.summary:
The volume of black-market tobacco in Australia fell 24 per cent over the past financial year, the first fall after five years of growth, according to Illicit Tobacco and E-cigarette Commission data reported by AAP. The commission said the market may have shrunk by up to 1,438 tonnes, though its exact size cannot be measured.

Australian Border Force seized more than 730 tonnes of illegal tobacco in the first quarter of this financial year, a record, AAP reported. Assistant Customs Minister Julian Hill said enforcement was working. The Coalition and One Nation have proposed cutting tobacco excise by 80 and 75 per cent respectively; the government says that would raise smoking rates.
keyFacts: Illicit tobacco volume fell 24 per cent last financial year
Border Force seized a record 730-plus tonnes in one quarter
Coalition and One Nation propose deep excise cuts; government opposes

articles.title: Lowy survey finds two in three Australians think AI risks outweigh benefits
articles.summary:
Sixty-five per cent of Australians said the risks of artificial intelligence outweigh its benefits in an October survey by the Lowy Institute, unchanged from March and up from 52 per cent in 2024, AAP reported. The share who said benefits outweigh risks fell to 33 per cent.

Report author Charles Lyons-Jones said the concerns sat against a weak economic backdrop, according to AAP. Fewer than a quarter of respondents were comfortable with Australian businesses using Chinese AI, compared with 36 per cent for US-made AI. Lowy's main annual poll, released in June, recorded 64 per cent saying risks outweighed benefits.
keyFacts: 65 per cent say AI risks outweigh benefits, Lowy's October survey found
Up from 52 per cent in 2024
Under a quarter comfortable with businesses using Chinese AI

articles.title: Third US carrier arrives in Middle East; Iran says it will not wait to be attacked
articles.summary:
The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group entered the area covered by US Central Command on Sunday, joining two other carrier groups already in the region, according to a US official cited by Al Jazeera and Gulf News. Gulf News, citing ABC News in the US, reported more than 20 Navy vessels are supporting a blockade of Iranian ports.

Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi told state news agency IRNA that Tehran would not wait for the US to strike first, and suggested Washington could be using diplomacy to prepare another attack. Israel National News reported President Donald Trump said in an interview he had no hesitation about renewed strikes, while Reuters reported he was weighing a delay.
keyFacts: USS Theodore Roosevelt is the third US carrier group in the region
More than 20 US Navy vessels support a blockade of Iranian ports, reports say
Iran's deputy foreign minister said Tehran will not wait to be attacked

articles.title: Iran says supertanker carrying two million barrels sank after hitting mine in Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said a supertanker carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil sank in the southern Persian Gulf after striking a mine and catching fire in the Strait of Hormuz, AFP reported via RTÉ. The Guards said two tankers travelling on what they called an unauthorised route had hit mines. They did not name the vessels.

There was no independent confirmation of the sinking, according to RTÉ. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said the extent of the damage was unknown but the crew were safe. The US military recently said it had cleared mines from the strait's main shipping routes. Iran has heavily restricted traffic through the strait since the war began in late February.
keyFacts: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say a supertanker with over two million barrels sank
The sinking has not been independently confirmed
UKMTO said the crew were safe

articles.title: Coles investigates cybersecurity incident, says no evidence customer data was taken
articles.summary:
Supermarket group Coles told the ASX on Monday morning it was investigating a cybersecurity incident, ABC News reported. The company said it had not identified any evidence that customer, staff or supplier data had been compromised or removed, and that stores and operations were continuing.

Coles said it was working with global cybersecurity experts to contain and secure its IT systems and would give further updates as appropriate, according to the ABC. It said customers did not need to take any action but should remain vigilant. A small number of customers were having problems with Liquorland click-and-collect orders. Coles did not give details of the nature of the incident.
keyFacts: Coles disclosed the incident in an ASX statement on Monday
The company says it has found no evidence data was taken
Some Liquorland click-and-collect orders were affected

articles.title: Australia, Canada, Italy and UK urge Israel to let 150,000 tents into Gaza
articles.summary:
The foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, Italy and the United Kingdom issued a joint statement saying the humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire as winter arrives, according to the text published by Global Affairs Canada. The statement says 150,000 tents and other supplies are being held at the border and prevented from entering.

The four governments urged Israel to open crossings and allow immediate and unimpeded humanitarian access, and called on all parties to implement the Comprehensive Plan for Gaza and respect the ceasefire. Foreign Minister Penny Wong said severe weather and heavy rain were worsening conditions, ABC News reported. Israel's response was not reported in the sources reviewed.
keyFacts: Joint statement by Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK
Says 150,000 tents are held at Gaza's border
Urges Israel to open crossings and parties to respect the ceasefire

articles.title: China's factory output and retail sales growth slow more than expected in October
articles.summary:
China's industrial output rose 4.8 per cent in October from a year earlier, below the 5.3 per cent forecast in a Reuters poll and down from 5.5 per cent in September, according to official data reported by Reuters via The Standard. Retail sales grew 0.4 per cent, against expectations of 0.8 per cent.

Fixed-asset investment fell 8.1 per cent in the first ten months of the year, a steeper decline than the 7 per cent forecast, Reuters reported. New home prices fell 2.4 per cent over the year, Investing.com said. The surveyed urban unemployment rate eased to 5.1 per cent. China is Australia's largest trading partner.
keyFacts: Industrial output up 4.8% year on year, below 5.3% forecast
Retail sales up 0.4%, against 0.8% expected
Fixed-asset investment down 8.1% in January–October

articles.title: Japan's economy contracts in the September quarter
articles.summary:
Japan's economy shrank at an annualised rate of 0.1 per cent in the July–September quarter, according to preliminary government figures reported by ABC News and ForexLive. Economists had expected growth of about 0.3 per cent, ForexLive reported.

ForexLive said weaker exports and consumer spending weighed on the result, while other reports pointed to a rise in imports. The figures were released on Monday, the same day as Chinese data showing slower-than-expected growth in factory output and retail sales. Japan is one of Australia's largest export markets, and the result follows earlier pressure on Japanese households from higher energy costs, reports said.
keyFacts: Japan's GDP fell at an annualised 0.1% in the September quarter
Forecasts had pointed to growth of about 0.3%
Exports and consumer spending weighed, reports said

articles.title: ASX 200 falls 0.4 per cent for third straight loss as miners decline
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 index closed 37.5 points, or 0.4 per cent, lower at 9,044.7 on Monday, its third consecutive daily fall, according to ShareCafe. Mining stocks were the main drag, while real estate and technology shares edged higher.

ShareCafe linked continued caution over artificial intelligence stocks to the leadership upheaval at Nvidia. ABC News reported online retailer Adore Beauty fell 36 per cent to a record low after cutting its guidance, and that the Australian dollar traded at about 67.6 US cents. Coles disclosed a cybersecurity incident during the session, and IDP Education rejected a third takeover proposal from Blackstone.
keyFacts: ASX 200 closed down 0.4% at 9,044.7
Miners led the falls; real estate and tech edged up
Australian dollar near 67.6 US cents

articles.title: IDP Education rejects Blackstone's third takeover proposal at $3 a share
articles.summary:
IDP Education's board rejected a third unsolicited proposal from private equity firm Blackstone of $3.00 a share, which valued the international student placement and IELTS testing company at about $835 million, Times Higher Education reported. Investing.com put the value at $US564.5 million.

The board said the offer substantially undervalued the company and was opportunistic, citing its student placement platform, its co-ownership of IELTS and a cost-cutting program it said was not yet fully realised, according to Times Higher Education. It said granting due diligence would be a distraction. IDP shares traded at about $2.50 on Monday. Blackstone's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Blackstone's third proposal was $3.00 a share
IDP's board says the bid undervalues the company
Shares traded near $2.50 on Monday

articles.title: Yemen's Houthis release 600 detainees in largest unilateral release of the war
articles.summary:
Yemen's Houthi movement released 600 detainees on Sunday, the International Committee of the Red Cross said, according to The New Arab. The ICRC said its teams spoke with each person released to assess their health and needs. Al Jazeera described those freed as war detainees.

Abdelkader al-Mourtada, who heads the Houthis' prisoner affairs committee in Sanaa, called it the largest unilateral release in the conflict and said 2,612 prisoners had been freed previously, The New Arab reported. He accused Saudi Arabia of blocking progress on exchanges; Saudi Arabia's response was not reported. The UN says more than 1,600 people have been killed since fighting resumed in July.
keyFacts: ICRC says Houthis freed 600 detainees on Sunday
Houthi official calls it the largest unilateral release of the conflict
UN says over 1,600 killed since fighting resumed in July

articles.title: Russian drone attack on Odesa region cuts power to 41,000 families, officials say
articles.summary:
Russia launched 132 long-range drones at Ukraine overnight into Sunday, and Ukraine's air force said 106 were intercepted, the Kyiv Independent reported. Odesa regional governor Oleh Kiper described a mass attack on the region that hit an energy facility run by DTEK and temporarily left about 41,000 families without power.

Six people were injured in the Odesa region and homes, a school, a gas pipeline and an administrative building were damaged, according to the Kyiv Independent. Across Ukraine, four people were killed and 69 injured over the previous day, it reported. Ukrinform said the head of Odesa's city military administration reported a further attack later on Sunday that damaged infrastructure. Russia did not comment in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: Russia launched 132 drones; Ukraine says 106 were downed
About 41,000 Odesa-region families temporarily lost power
Four killed and 69 injured across Ukraine over a day

articles.title: Bird flu outbreak in poultry could cost economy up to $6.2b, EY modelling finds
articles.summary:
An outbreak of H5N1 bird flu in Australia's commercial poultry industry could reduce real GDP by between $0.7 billion and $6.2 billion over 2026 to 2028, according to EY-Parthenon modelling reported by AAP. It estimated between about 500 and 5,600 full-time jobs could be lost.

The modelling suggested a $6.40 carton of eggs could rise to about $11.20 and a rotisserie chicken from $13 to about $22.75, AAP reported. H5N1 was first confirmed in Australia on 19 June. As of 12 November there had been more than 730 confirmed detections in wildlife and none in commercial poultry, according to AAP.
keyFacts: EY modelling puts potential GDP loss at $0.7b to $6.2b
Egg and chicken prices could rise sharply in an outbreak
No H5N1 detections in commercial poultry so far, AAP says

articles.title: Solomon Islands opposition accuses Australia of 'chequebook diplomacy' over MP grants
articles.summary:
The Solomon Islands opposition has accused Australia of chequebook diplomacy after reports that Prime Minister Matthew Wale's government gave MPs discretionary grants of up to SBD1 million, about $180,000 each, from a bank account labelled AusAID, ABC News reported.

The ABC said the account belongs to the Solomon Islands government rather than to Australia. The reported grants came from that account, according to the ABC. Responses from the Australian Government and Mr Wale's office to the opposition's claim were not detailed in the reports reviewed. The claim was reported in the ABC's federal politics coverage on Monday, while Prime Minister Anthony Albanese was in Manila for the ASEAN summit.
keyFacts: Opposition alleges 'chequebook diplomacy' by Australia
MPs reportedly received grants of up to SBD1 million each
ABC says the 'AusAID' account belongs to the Solomon Islands government

articles.title: Lawyer says public may never learn result of Tasmanian integrity probe into Ogilvie
articles.summary:
A lawyer for former Tasmanian minister Madeleine Ogilvie told a state parliamentary committee the public may never learn the outcome of the Integrity Commission's investigation into her, ABC News reported. The probe, now nearly five years old, concerns an alleged conflict over a 2021 election commitment to fund a rowing club pontoon.

Chris Gunson SC said the Supreme Court ruled last week that the commission cannot table its investigation reports in parliament, according to the ABC. Greens MLC Cassy O'Connor said there was no information in the public domain about the investigation. Ms Ogilvie has previously contested the commission's process in court. The commission's response was not reported.
keyFacts: Integrity Commission probe into Ogilvie began nearly five years ago
Supreme Court ruled the commission cannot table reports in parliament
Concerns a 2021 pledge to fund a rowing club pontoon

leftOut.title: Iran repeats it will not send enriched uranium abroad; US keeps focus on sanctions
leftOut.summary:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, said again this week that none of Iran's enriched nuclear material will leave the country. He first made the statement publicly on 20 October during a visit by Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said economic pressure, including a naval blockade, has reduced the need for major combat. Axios first reported in August that Rubio told allies the US was shifting from strikes to sanctions, without ruling out force if Iran attacks first.
keyFacts: Iran says its enriched material is for use only inside the country
US strategy: naval blockade plus Treasury sanctions
Both positions have been stated before

leftOut.title: Digital duty of care bill awaits Senate committee report due 20 November
leftOut.summary:
The Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026 passed the House of Representatives on 28 October and is now before the Senate. It would place a legal duty on online services, including social media, search engines and generative AI services, to take reasonable steps to keep Australians safe, with extra protections for under-18s.

Companies that breach the duty could face penalties of up to about $109 million. The government has backed changes aimed at AI chatbots that simulate emotional intimacy with children. The Greens want stronger penalties.
keyFacts: Introduced by Communications Minister Anika Wells
Passed the House on 28 October
Senate committee report due 20 November

leftOut.title: Pope Leo draws an estimated 2.5 million to Buenos Aires Mass on first papal visit to Argentina since 1987
leftOut.summary:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass in Buenos Aires on 9 November that officials estimated drew 2.5 million people, the largest gathering of his papacy. The same day he met victims of clergy abuse. He celebrated Mass in Córdoba on 10 November and visited Luján on 11 November.

It is the first papal visit to Argentina since 1987. The 12-day trip also covers Uruguay and Peru and ends on 17 November.
keyFacts: Argentina leg ran 8–11 November
The Pope met President Javier Milei during the visit
Next stop: Peru

leftOut.title: David Walliams faces further allegations; he denies wrongdoing
leftOut.summary:
Comedian and children's author David Walliams faced further allegations this week of inappropriate behaviour towards young women, in reporting by The Guardian and ITV. HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025 after an internal investigation, and in September 2026 it stopped publishing his back catalogue.

Walliams strongly denies behaving inappropriately. His spokesperson has said he was never told of the allegations or given a chance to respond to the publisher's investigation.
keyFacts: HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025
His back catalogue was dropped in September 2026
He denies all allegations

leftOut.title: Harry and Meghan speak at European Parliament event on social media harms to children
leftOut.summary:
Prince Harry and Meghan attended an event at the European Parliament in Brussels on 10 November. It opened a memorial installation showing images of 50 children who died after harm they suffered on social media. Parliament President Roberta Metsola was also due to speak.

It was the couple's first public appearance since the allegations against Meghan's father emerged. Harry has campaigned on the risks of social media and AI chatbots for young people.
keyFacts: Event at the European Parliament, Brussels
The installation is called the Lost Screen Memorial
Harry spoke on AI chatbots and children in September

leftOut.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent moved to military base over Iranian threats, sources say
leftOut.summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved to live on a military base because of threats from Iran, ABC News (US) reported on Wednesday, citing multiple unnamed sources familiar with the situation. He had reportedly been living in Washington's Georgetown area.

The report said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio also live on military bases while in Washington. The Secret Service, which protects Bessent, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The move has not been officially confirmed.
keyFacts: The report relies on unnamed sources
ABC News (US) described the story as developing
No official statement had been issued

leftOut.title: Russian strikes kill several people and cut power in eight Ukrainian regions
leftOut.summary:
Russian attacks on 10 and 11 November killed at least four people and injured more than 20 across several Ukrainian regions, according to regional officials cited by Ukrainian news agency UNN. Zaporizhzhia's governor Ivan Fedorov reported one death and 15 injuries, and Donetsk officials reported two deaths.

UNN reported power outages in eight regions, with emergency cuts in Kharkiv after a missile strike damaged garages and cars there. The attacks came as Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with a prisoner exchange agreement.
keyFacts: Odesa's governor said a 70-year-old woman died of her injuries
Donetsk officials reported 661 evacuations
Zhytomyr reported damage to energy and transport sites

leftOut.title: Human remains found in sofa dumped in Sydney bushland at Lane Cove North
leftOut.summary:
NSW Police said a man found human remains inside a storage sofa dumped in bushland off Avian Crescent, Lane Cove North, on Wednesday afternoon, the ABC reported. A forensic examination found they were the torso of an adult man. Police said the remains had been there for at least a couple of days.

Superintendent Paul Devaney said police were working to identify the man and find out how he died. He said there was no sign of foul play in Lane Cove and residents were not under threat. Police used a cadaver dog, a line search and aerial surveillance.
keyFacts: The man has not been formally identified
A post-mortem examination will be held
Police are checking the missing persons register

leftOut.title: Man who drove fugitive Hussein Chamas across Australia faces sentencing in Darwin
leftOut.summary:
Irish national Stephen Roche faced a sentencing hearing in the NT Supreme Court on Thursday after pleading guilty to attempting to pervert the course of justice, the ABC reported. He drove fugitive Hussein Chamas about 4,680 kilometres in a rented van before Chamas was intercepted by Border Force in the Arafura Sea.

The prosecution said jail was the only appropriate penalty. Roche's lawyer argued that 123 days already spent on remand was enough, citing his health and remorse. The court heard Roche was to be paid $30,000.
keyFacts: Sentence is due on 1 December
Chamas was jailed in August on drug charges
Roche was arrested in January 2025

leftOut.title: Missing teenager found alive after six nights in Gippsland bush
leftOut.summary:
A 17-year-old who went missing while camping at Walhalla East in Victoria's Gippsland was found alive on Thursday morning, Victoria Police said, according to the ABC. A police helicopter crew spotted him in a dry riverbed about two kilometres east of Stoney Creek.

Police said he had fallen down a steep embankment two days earlier and could not walk. He had cuts and severe sunburn and was taken to Latrobe Regional Hospital. More than 80 volunteers had joined the search, along with police divers, the dog squad and helicopters.
keyFacts: He went missing on 6 November
Walhalla East is about 180 km east of Melbourne
He is being monitored in hospital

leftOut.title: One killed, four injured in shooting at Washington DC gym; gunman dead
leftOut.summary:
A gunman shot five people at and near a gym in Washington DC's Logan Circle neighbourhood on Thursday morning local time, killing one, police said, according to Al Jazeera and CBS News. The area is about 1.6 kilometres north of the White House.

Police said the suspect later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound after a standoff. Interim Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said the shooting appeared to stem from a dispute with a condominium homeowners association. Nearby schools and apartment buildings were locked down during the search. A local councillor named a suspect, but police had not formally confirmed the identity in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: The shooting began about 8am local time
Federal ATF agents assisted DC police
Police point to a residential dispute as a motive

leftOut.title: Perth inquest hears triple-zero call before 2024 double murder was wrongly graded
leftOut.summary:
A WA coronial inquest has heard that a triple-zero call made before the May 2024 shooting deaths of Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl at their Perth home was graded priority two rather than priority one, AAP reported. Counsel assisting said Mark Bombara shot both women and then himself.

WA Police Commander Jason Longhorn told the inquest he believed the priority two grading was incorrect. Superintendent Andrew Wilson said officers had not assessed the risk correctly and that eight officers were disciplined. A lawyer for the family said the women had been targeted as proxies for Bombara's family. The inquest is continuing.
keyFacts: The killings occurred on 24 May 2024
Eight officers were disciplined
The inquest continues

leftOut.title: AFP charges two men over alleged threats to federal politicians
leftOut.summary:
The Australian Federal Police charged two men with using a carriage service to menace, harass or cause offence over alleged threats to politicians, AAP reported. A 43-year-old man was arrested in the Moreton Bay area north of Brisbane on Thursday, and a 67-year-old man was arrested in Melbourne on Wednesday and faces three counts.

Both men were granted conditional bail and are due in court in January and February. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said police charge about one person a week for threatening parliamentarians. The allegations have not been tested in court, and neither man had entered a plea in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: One man was charged in Queensland, one in Victoria
Both were granted conditional bail
The AFP says it charges about one person a week over such threats

leftOut.title: Trial begins over alleged murder of Quambatook woman in dispute over pool work
leftOut.summary:
Brian Robert Barnes, 68, has pleaded not guilty in the Victorian Supreme Court to murdering 70-year-old Merril Kelly at her home in Quambatook, in north-west Victoria, in January 2025, AAP reported.

Crown prosecutor Patrick Bourke KC alleged Barnes was angry about unpaid pool work and attacked Kelly before taking her body to a cemetery and setting it alight. He said an autopsy showed she died before the fire. Defence barrister David Cronin SC told the jury Barnes did not cause her death and that someone else may have inflicted the fatal injuries. The trial before Justice James Elliott is continuing.
keyFacts: Barnes has pleaded not guilty
Prosecutors allege a dispute over pool work
The trial is continuing

leftOut.title: Pancreatic cancer advocate Cherie Dear named Victorian Australian of the Year
leftOut.summary:
Cherie Dear, who co-founded pancreatic cancer charity Dare to Hope with her late husband, former Hawthorn player Paul Dear, has been named Victoria's 2027 Australian of the Year, ABC News reported.

The other Victorian winners are autism researcher Wenn Lawson as Senior Australian of the Year, Ryan Brigham of Health in Focus as Young Australian of the Year, and Gavin Hynam, who has donated 19 cars to people in need, as Local Hero. The four will join other state and territory recipients in Canberra, where the national winners will be announced on 25 January.
keyFacts: Four Victorian award recipients were named
National awards are on 25 January
State winners become national finalists

leftOut.title: Kalyn Ponga and Stacey Waaka win rugby league's Golden Boot awards
leftOut.summary:
New Zealand's Kalyn Ponga has won the men's International Rugby League Golden Boot for 2026 and compatriot Stacey Waaka won the women's award, AAP reported. The awards were presented at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane on Thursday night.

Ponga broke his forearm in New Zealand's 24-20 World Cup loss to Australia and returned 23 days later. Waaka scored nine tries in four World Cup matches. England's Rob Hawkins won the wheelchair Golden Boot. AAP said voting did not include Sunday's World Cup final.
keyFacts: Ponga is 28
Waaka scored nine World Cup tries
Rob Hawkins won the wheelchair award

leftOut.title: Players' union asks for Socceroos friendly in Jordan to be moved over safety
leftOut.summary:
Professional Footballers Australia has asked Football Australia to reschedule or relocate the Socceroos' planned friendly against Jordan in Amman because of security concerns, AAP reported. PFA chief executive Beau Busch said players overwhelmingly supported the request.

Australia are due to play Qatar in Doha before travelling to Amman four days later. Indonesia has cancelled its 13 November friendly in Amman. AAP said the Asian Cup was postponed after an attack on Riyadh airport attributed to the Houthis. Winger Awer Mabil said he would travel if selected. The squad announcement has been delayed to the weekend.
keyFacts: The PFA wants the match moved or rescheduled
Indonesia cancelled its game in Amman
Football Australia had not announced a decision

leftOut.title: Perth Bears say they are confident of signing Matt Burton
leftOut.summary:
Perth Bears general manager Gareth Holmes said on Thursday he was hopeful of signing Canterbury and NSW State of Origin player Matt Burton within days, AAP reported. Burton had not confirmed any move.

Holmes spoke at the launch of the new NRL club's away jumper at North Sydney Oval and said Burton had decisions to make. Burton visited the club this week. AAP said the Bears can offer a salary-cap allowance of 20 per cent granted by Australian Rugby League Commission chair Peter V'landys in August.
keyFacts: The signing is not confirmed
Burton visited the club this week
The Bears join the NRL as an expansion team

leftOut.title: David Jones staff and union react to planned closure of 19 stores
leftOut.summary:
Thousands of David Jones' 6,000 staff are affected by receivers FTI Consulting's plan, announced on Wednesday, for 19 stores in Australia and New Zealand to trade only until the end of December, AAP reported.

NSW retail union secretary Bernie Smith blamed management decisions for the collapse. Charles Lloyd Jones, a member of the founding family, told AAP that retailers without a distinctive offer were forced to compete on price. The retailer lost $95.5 million in 2024-25. The store closures were reported in an earlier update; this report adds reactions but no new decisions.
keyFacts: 19 stores will close after December
The chain employs about 6,000 people
It lost $95.5m in 2024-25

leftOut.title: Victorian business conditions weakest of any state ahead of election, NAB survey shows
leftOut.summary:
NAB's monthly business survey showed business conditions in Victoria fell to minus 6 in October, the lowest of any state and below the national reading of minus 1, AAP reported. NAB senior economist Gareth Spence linked part of the fall to uncertainty before the 28 November state election.

AAP also cited the Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer confidence index, which fell 2.7 per cent to a four-year low. Westpac's Matthew Hassan pointed to petrol prices near $2.40 a litre, inflation of 4.3 per cent and the RBA's rate rise to 4.85 per cent. Both surveys were released earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Victorian conditions index: minus 6
National conditions index: minus 1
Consumer confidence is at a four-year low

leftOut.title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon found guilty of sexually assaulting 13-year-old
leftOut.summary:
A NSW Supreme Court jury found former Pittwater MP Rory Amon guilty of the sexual assault and indecent assault of a 13-year-old boy in 2017, the ABC reported. The jury deliberated for about four hours.

The court heard Amon met the boy through a dating app. Amon had argued he believed the boy was 17. He remains on bail, and sentencing is listed for later this month. At an earlier trial in March, Amon was acquitted of most charges and the jury could not agree on two counts.
keyFacts: The jury deliberated about four hours
The offences occurred in 2017
Sentencing is listed for later this month

leftOut.title: Cummins rejects Khawaja's claim that whole team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plan
leftOut.summary:
Australian Test captain Pat Cummins rejected former teammate Usman Khawaja's claim, made in his memoir, that the entire team knew of the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering plan, the ABC reported. Cummins said he did not know sandpaper was being used.

Cummins said Khawaja had been careless with people's reputations and that legal advice suggested some claims could be defamatory, though he would not take action. He also said the bans given to three players were too harsh. Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation.
keyFacts: The comments came at a press conference in Sydney
Cricket Australia will not reopen its investigation
Cummins said he would not sue

leftOut.title: Victoria Police will not charge four Sydney Swans players, citing insufficient evidence
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police said it would not lay criminal charges against Sydney Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Nick Blakey over an alleged incident at a Melbourne hotel in August, citing insufficient evidence after legal advice, the ABC reported.

Police noted an ongoing civil matter and declined further comment. Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich said the players could now move forward, and the club said it stood by its decision to stand them down. Lawyers for three women are pursuing civil claims.
keyFacts: Police cited insufficient evidence
The alleged incident occurred in August
Civil claims are continuing

leftOut.title: Prosecutors oppose bail for Darwin teenager charged with terrorism offence
leftOut.summary:
A Darwin teenage girl charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts appeared in court on Friday, AAP reported. Prosecutor Hadi Mazloum alleged her diary named a student she wanted dead and that she shared a plan to shoot at a school, and argued the risk to the community was too high for bail.

Her lawyer cited significant psychological circumstances and sought a supervised community-based order. The judge adjourned the bail application to Monday. A 14-year-old boy was arrested with her on 3 November.
keyFacts: She was arrested on 3 November
The arrest followed a joint AFP, NT Police and ASIO operation
Bail will be decided on Monday

leftOut.title: Analysis estimates Victorian Labor has outspent Liberals sixfold on online ads
leftOut.summary:
An analysis by digital campaign platform Populares estimates Victorian Labor and its candidates have spent $3.1 million on online advertising since August, compared with just over $500,000 by the Liberals and about $21,000 by One Nation, the ABC reported. The figures are upper-range estimates from platform disclosures and exclude other media.

The ABC said Labor, the Liberals and the Greens did not respond. An Australia Institute representative said the campaign had seen unprecedented use of AI content and deepfakes.
keyFacts: Labor spending estimated at $3.1 million
Liberal spending just over $500,000
Figures exclude TV and print

leftOut.title: ABC reports US has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government over rare earths
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government ahead of the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, the ABC reported, citing a State Department document that lists countering China and access to rare earth resources among the goals.

The talks followed the detention of a former American Chamber of Commerce head at Yangon airport in June. A Lowy Institute analyst described it as hostage diplomacy, and a human rights advocate criticised the talks. The US has previously accused Myanmar's military of genocide.
keyFacts: China controls about 90 per cent of rare earth output, an analyst said
The ASEAN summit is in the Philippines
The piece is an ABC analysis

leftOut.title: 1960 paper had predicted population would become infinite on 13 November 2026
leftOut.summary:
A 1960 paper in the journal Science predicted world population would approach infinity on 13 November 2026, based on a formula drawn from historical fertility and death rates, the ABC reported. The date was chosen to fall on lead author Heinz von Foerster's birthday.

An economist quoted said the projections held until about the 1980s. Global population growth peaked at about 2.3 per cent a year in 1963, and the UN projects population will peak at just over 10 billion in about 60 years.
keyFacts: The paper was published in 1960
Growth peaked in 1963
The UN projects a peak just over 10 billion

leftOut.title: Olympic cyclist Rohan Dennis admits breaching good behaviour bond
leftOut.summary:
Olympic medallist Rohan Dennis admitted in the South Australian District Court that he breached a good behaviour bond, AAP reported. The bond, imposed in 2025 over the December 2023 crash that killed his wife Melissa Hoskins, carries a suspended 17-month jail term.

Dennis was caught driving while disqualified in June, with two children in the car. Judge Emily Telfer ordered a supervision compliance report and adjourned the matter to 1 February.
keyFacts: The breach was admitted on Friday
The bond carries a 17-month term
The matter returns on 1 February

leftOut.title: Man dies in workplace incident in Adelaide's north-east
leftOut.summary:
A 26-year-old man died at the scene of a workplace incident on Leopold Street, Vista, in Adelaide's north-eastern suburbs on Friday, South Australia Police said, according to the ABC. Emergency services were called at about 12.15pm.

SafeWork SA said it had been notified and sent an investigator and an inspector. SA Power Networks workers were seen examining a power pole nearby. Police will prepare a report for the coroner. No cause has been stated.
keyFacts: The man was 26
SafeWork SA is investigating
A report will go to the coroner

leftOut.title: Guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimands Hegseth's group during photos
leftOut.summary:
A video shows a sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery asking Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's group to maintain silence and respect while they were laughing during photographs on Veterans Day, Al Jazeera reported.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said the sentinel had responded correctly and that the department honours the military's sacrifices. The incident came a day after House Republicans blocked a vote on articles of impeachment against Hegseth.
keyFacts: The incident was on 11 November
The Pentagon said the guard acted correctly
House Republicans blocked an impeachment vote

leftOut.title: Westpac says it is financing 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects
leftOut.summary:
Westpac chief executive Anthony Miller told a parliamentary inquiry on Thursday that the bank was financing 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects than 18 months ago, and that each dollar lent was delivering fewer homes, AAP reported. He said replacing staff with AI was not the bank's focus.

ANZ chief Nuno Matos said he could not guarantee there would be no job losses from AI. ABS data released on Wednesday showed investor home loans fell a record 30.6 per cent.
keyFacts: Westpac's construction financing is down 30 per cent
CBA and NAB appeared on Friday
Investor loans fell a record 30.6 per cent

leftOut.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield satellite service speeds again restricted
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speed restrictions on Starshield, the military version of the Starlink satellite service, were again hampering Ukraine's interception of Russian jet-powered drones, AAP reported.

The report also restated that Abu Dhabi talks earlier in the week agreed a large prisoner exchange, which Russia's TASS said could happen within two to three weeks. Ukraine said it shot down 89 of 123 drones overnight, and one person was killed in Kyiv. The figures could not be independently verified.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy posted the claim on Thursday
TASS said a swap could come within weeks
Ukraine said 89 of 123 drones were downed

leftOut.title: Rubio says UK and European nations should be part of Ukraine peace talks
leftOut.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that the UK and other European countries should have a place at negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, AAP reported. He described the Abu Dhabi talks as productive but said much work remained.

Ukraine's president called the talks constructive and substantive, the first since February. Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov said he favoured a broader European security framework being agreed first.
keyFacts: The remarks were made at the G7 in Paris
The Abu Dhabi talks were the first since February
Lavrov wants a wider security framework first

leftOut.title: Former police officer denies desperation in Paddington murder trial evidence
leftOut.summary:
Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, who has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in February 2024 and claims self-defence, continued his evidence on Thursday, AAP reported.

Under cross-examination about a long message he sent to Baird claiming a cancer diagnosis, he acknowledged parts were untrue but denied being desperate or obsessed. He also admitted posting a false image online about a relationship. The trial continues.
keyFacts: He has pleaded not guilty
Thursday was his sixth day of evidence
The deaths occurred on 19 February 2024

leftOut.title: CBA and NAB chiefs to face parliamentary hearings after fee and wage cases
leftOut.summary:
Commonwealth Bank chief Matt Comyn and NAB chief Andrew Irvine were due to appear before parliamentary hearings on Friday, AAP reported, after NAB agreed to repay $169 million to 66,000 underpaid staff and ASIC began proceedings against CBA over $8.5 million in undisclosed business fees.

Committee chair Ed Husic, a Labor MP, criticised NAB's plans to move about 180 roles offshore. Westpac's chief disclosed a 28 per cent gender pay gap at the hearings.
keyFacts: Hearings continued on Friday
NAB is repaying $169 million
ASIC is suing CBA over $8.5 million in fees

leftOut.title: Ottawa agency weighs artificially freezing part of Rideau Canal skateway
leftOut.summary:
Canada's National Capital Commission is considering refrigerating a 900-metre stretch of the Rideau Canal in downtown Ottawa so it can be used for skating more often, The Canadian Press reported. The commission's chief operating officer, Tobi Nussbaum, told CBC News that a feasibility study proposed using refrigeration pipes.

Nussbaum said the number of skating days could triple, but not before 2030. The canal opened for only 10 days in 2024 and did not open to skaters in 2023, according to The Canadian Press. The study links the shorter seasons to warmer winters.
keyFacts: Stretch under study is 900 metres long
Skating days could triple, the commission says
Not expected before 2030

leftOut.title: Republicans acknowledge midterm defeat but few call for a break with Trump
leftOut.summary:
Republican lawmakers have acknowledged that voters rejected them in the midterm elections but have shown little interest in breaking with President Donald Trump, AP reported. Representative Richard Hudson, who led the House Republican campaign arm, said voters felt costs were too high. House Speaker Mike Johnson said voters made the wrong choice.

Senator Josh Hawley blamed cuts to rural healthcare, and Representative Lauren Boebert said the party had collectively failed, according to AP. Democrats flipped more than 40 Republican-held House seats. The piece is an analysis of reactions rather than a report of a new event.
keyFacts: Democrats flipped more than 40 House seats
Hudson led the House Republican campaign arm
Analysis piece drawing on lawmakers' comments

leftOut.title: US travel restrictions keep some African contestants out of Miss Universe
leftOut.summary:
Some contestants from African countries may miss the Miss Universe pageant in Puerto Rico on 24 November because of visa problems linked to US travel restrictions, The Daily Beast reported. Miss Universe Zambia organisers said their contestant, Pamela Mubanga, had been forced to withdraw.

Zimbabwe's Roseanna Hall said her visa approval had stalled, and South Sudan's Amylia Deng said her participation was uncertain, according to The Daily Beast. The restrictions on nationals of a number of countries took effect on 1 January 2026. The outlet said it had sought comment from the State Department.
keyFacts: Pageant final is on 24 November
Zambia's contestant has withdrawn
Restrictions took effect on 1 January 2026

leftOut.title: London police open investigation into David Walliams over sexual offence allegations
leftOut.summary:
London's Metropolitan Police said it had received several allegations of non-recent serious sexual offences involving a man in his 50s and had opened an investigation, ITV News and ABC News reported, identifying the man as author David Walliams. The allegations are separate from a joint ITV and Guardian investigation published earlier in the week.

Walliams denies the allegations and says he has not broken the law. Detective Superintendent Mike Cagney is leading the inquiry. Police have not said how many offences were reported or when they allegedly occurred.
keyFacts: Allegations are described as non-recent
Walliams denies any wrongdoing
Separate from the ITV and Guardian reports

leftOut.title: Six more women make misconduct allegations against Russell Brand, Times reports
leftOut.summary:
Six more women have accused comedian Russell Brand of sexual misconduct between 2005 and 2013, according to a report in The Times cited by NME. The Times said it had taken extensive steps to corroborate the claims and had not paid any sources.

Brand was convicted last week of rape and three counts of sexual assault and was sentenced on 9 November to 10 years and six months in prison, NME reported. He has previously denied wrongdoing. London police are investigating two further rape allegations.
keyFacts: Allegations cover 2005 to 2013
Brand was sentenced on 9 November
He has previously denied wrongdoing

leftOut.title: Socceroos beat Asian champions Qatar 3-0 in Doha friendly
leftOut.summary:
Australia beat Qatar 3-0 in an international friendly in Doha, AAP reported. Riley McGree, Tete Yengi and Nestory Irankunda scored in the first half, and Qatar had a late goal ruled out for offside.

Coach Tony Popovic made several changes and gave debuts to four players: Eli Adams, Sam Klein, Kasey Bos and Diesel Herrington, according to AAP. Australia had 14 shots to Qatar's three. The Socceroos play Jordan in Doha on Tuesday, Wednesday Australian time.
keyFacts: All three goals came in the first half
Four players made debuts
Jordan match follows on Tuesday in Doha

leftOut.title: Newsom says he will decide on a 2028 presidential run in early January
leftOut.summary:
California Governor Gavin Newsom said he would decide in early January whether to run for president in 2028, the Sacramento Bee and Fox News reported. He made the comments to Turkey's Anadolu Agency at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya.

Newsom, who leaves office in January, has previously said he would consult his family first and would not run if former vice-president Kamala Harris entered the race. Harris has not commented publicly, according to the Sacramento Bee. Newsom said the recent midterm results would factor into his decision.
keyFacts: Decision due in early January
Newsom leaves office in January
Harris has not commented publicly

leftOut.title: Al Green says he will seek another House vote on impeaching Trump
leftOut.summary:
Democratic Congressman Al Green of Texas said on the House floor that he would call for a vote on impeaching President Donald Trump as early as next week, Breitbart News reported. Green said he has made similar calls at least six times.

Green linked the move to the recent failed attempt to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth. In September the House voted 232 to 147 to set aside an earlier Green impeachment resolution. The report did not include a response from the White House or House leaders.
keyFacts: Vote sought as early as next week
September resolution set aside 232-147
No White House response reported

leftOut.title: Trump promoted film tax bill while FAA ground stop was under way, TheWrap reports
leftOut.summary:
President Donald Trump posted support on Truth Social for a bipartisan bill offering federal incentives for film and television production while a nationwide FAA ground stop was in place on Friday, TheWrap reported. It said he had not publicly addressed the flight disruption at that time.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy had posted that a communication issue was behind the stoppage and that technicians were investigating, according to TheWrap. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the cause was not yet known but it was not a terrorist attack.
keyFacts: Trump backed a federal production incentive bill
Report says he had not addressed the stoppage
Officials said no terrorist link

leftOut.title: Albanese and Bowen caught on open microphone joking at COP31
leftOut.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Climate Change and Energy Minister Chris Bowen were recorded on an open microphone sharing a private joke at the COP31 climate summit in Türkiye, the ABC reported in a short video. The remark involved a crude reference.

The exchange came as Albanese left the summit for the ASEAN meeting in Manila, while Bowen stays on to lead negotiations, according to AAP. Neither minister had commented on the recording in the ABC's report.
keyFacts: Recorded at COP31 in Türkiye
ABC published a short video
No comment from either minister reported

leftOut.title: Australian aid workers recall 2001 detention by Taliban, 25 years on
leftOut.summary:
Two Australians held by the Taliban in 2001, Peter Bunch and Diana Thomas, have described their detention and rescue to AAP, 25 years after it ended. They were among eight Shelter Now International staff arrested in Kabul in August 2001 and accused of promoting Christianity.

After US strikes began and Northern Alliance forces advanced, the group was freed from a jail in Ghazni and later flown out by US special forces, reaching Pakistan on 15 November 2001, AAP reported. Former prime minister John Howard told AAP it was a dramatic time.
keyFacts: Eight aid workers were detained in 2001
Rescued by US special forces helicopter
Reached Pakistan on 15 November 2001

leftOut.title: Gunman's daughter gives evidence at Perth double murder inquest
leftOut.summary:
The daughter of Mark Bombara, who shot dead Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl at their Perth home in May 2024, gave evidence at the WA Coroners Court on Friday, AAP reported. Bombara, who had been looking for his estranged wife, then killed himself.

Ariel Bombara apologised to the victims' family and called for change on family and domestic violence, according to AAP. She criticised police for allowing her father to keep 13 firearms despite warnings. The acting state coroner will deliver findings at a later date.
keyFacts: Inquest is in the WA Coroners Court
Gunman held 13 firearms, court heard
Findings to be delivered later

leftOut.title: Greens seek end to fuel tax concession for private jets
leftOut.summary:
The Greens want parliament to end the lower excise rate on fuel used by private aircraft, with leader David Shoebridge citing Parliamentary Budget Office costings, AAP reported. The PBO estimated the change would raise $640 million in 2027 and $1.5 billion over the forward estimates.

Shoebridge said motorists pay 53.7 cents a litre in fuel tax compared with about 3.6 cents for jet owners, according to AAP. He named several high-profile jet owners as beneficiaries. The government's response was not included in the AAP report.
keyFacts: The proposal uses PBO costings
Shoebridge said drivers pay almost 15 times more tax per litre
The story was published before this update window

leftOut.title: Insurers receive more than 2,700 claims after storms in Queensland and NSW
leftOut.summary:
Insurers have received more than 2,700 claims after supercell storms hit south-east Queensland and northern NSW on Wednesday, the Insurance Council of Australia said, according to AAP. About 2,400 claims came from Queensland, and about 300 related to food spoiled during power cuts.

About 25,000 homes lost power on Thursday, and the SES received more than 300 calls, most in Logan, AAP reported. The Bureau of Meteorology warned of further storms and possible flash flooding over the weekend. Insurance Council chief Andrew Hall urged policyholders to keep receipts.
keyFacts: Gusts reached up to 120km/h in Logan
More than 20 schools were closed
The Darling Downs recorded 124mm in two hours

leftOut.title: Data show more small businesses raising prices after card surcharge ban
leftOut.summary:
A growing share of small businesses that previously added card surcharges have raised prices since the ban took effect on 1 October, according to payments company Tyro, AAP reported. Tyro's Nigel Lee said the share rose from 9.4 per cent in the first week to 12.4 per cent three weeks later.

Of those businesses, 61 per cent lifted prices by more than the old surcharge, Lee said. He expected more increases before the end of the year as rent, power, wage and interest costs rise. The ban is expected to save consumers about $1 billion over time.
keyFacts: Data cover 65,000 Tyro retail, hospitality and services clients
The surcharge ban began on 1 October
The report was published before this update window

leftOut.title: National working with children check database expands as SA joins
leftOut.summary:
A national system that tracks criminal records of Working With Children Check holders in near real time is expanding, with South Australia joining from Monday, AAP reported. The pilot already covers Commonwealth and ACT offences, but full coverage across all jurisdictions is not expected until 2028.

Attorney-General Michelle Rowland blamed differences between state systems for the timeline and said the government wanted to beat it. The 2015 royal commission into institutional child sexual abuse recommended a central database. The federal government has invested $37 million, and all jurisdictions have confirmed they will join.
keyFacts: The system is called the National Continuous Checking Capability
States must opt in, with no deadline
The report was published before this update window

leftOut.title: Equifax data point to rising business exits as David Jones closes stores
leftOut.summary:
Business exits rose 41.3 per cent year on year in the September quarter while new business entries fell more than 15 per cent, according to Equifax data reported by AAP alongside the David Jones collapse. Active tax defaults rose 25 per cent, the data showed.

Equifax's Brad Walters said smaller operators were borrowing to cover immediate overheads. David Jones entered administration and receivership on 5 November and plans to close 19 of its 38 stores. Retail groups forecast $7.2 billion in Black Friday and pre-Christmas spending.
keyFacts: Business-level insolvencies rose almost 17 per cent
Hospitality insolvencies eased 7 per cent
The piece is an analysis of retail conditions

leftOut.title: Man who escaped custody at Melbourne funeral arrested in far north Queensland
leftOut.summary:
Orijol Rukaj, 47, who escaped Corrections Victoria supervision during a visit to a Melbourne cemetery for his brother's funeral in April, has been arrested in Bamaga in far north Queensland, AAP reported. He had been on remand on drug importation charges.

Victoria Police said he would be extradited to Victoria within days, according to AAP. Police did not say how he travelled interstate. Officers have identified several overseas-based people they believe helped him escape. He has not yet faced the original charges in court.
keyFacts: Rukaj was on the run for about six months
He was arrested on Friday
Police earlier said he was unlikely to pose a risk to community safety

leftOut.title: Massie seeks Republican support for fourth House vote on Iran war powers
leftOut.summary:
Republican congressman Thomas Massie told Fox News Digital that a new resolution to limit President Donald Trump's military action against Iran could reach the House floor within the next few legislative days or around Christmas. It would be the fourth such attempt this year.

Republican Tom Barrett, who backed an earlier resolution, said he doubted more Republicans would join, according to Fox News, while Republican Jeff Van Drew said one or two might. Armed Services chair Mike Rogers will oppose it. No vote has been scheduled.
keyFacts: Earlier resolutions passed the House with some Republican votes
Massie is from Kentucky
No date has been set for a vote

leftOut.title: Son of former CIA director John Brennan charged over child abuse images
leftOut.summary:
Kyle Brennan, 40, the son of former CIA director John Brennan, has been charged in a federal complaint with transporting child sexual abuse material, Fox News reported. The case began with tips to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children in 2024, according to the report.

An FBI analysis of his phone allegedly found about 88 images, Fox News said, citing court documents. The allegations have not been tested in court. Responses from Brennan's lawyer, the Justice Department and the FBI were not included in the report.
keyFacts: The FBI's Washington field office is involved
Records tied uploads to an address in Warrenton, Virginia, Fox said
He was due to appear in federal court on Saturday US time

leftOut.title: US Atlantic regulator cuts menhaden catch limits for 2027 and 2028
leftOut.summary:
The Atlantic States Marine Fisheries Commission has voted to cut the East Coast menhaden catch limit by 9 per cent in 2027 and 17 per cent in 2028, adopting a compromise proposed by Maine, according to the Maine Monitor and the Associated Press. The limit falls from 186,840 tonnes in 2026 to 155,000 tonnes in 2028.

The commission also cut the Chesapeake Bay harvest cap by about a third, the Baltimore Banner reported. More than 48,000 public comments were received, most favouring a deeper cut. Fishing industry groups opposed the cap, while conservation groups said it did not go far enough.
keyFacts: Menhaden are a key food for striped bass and ospreys
Virginia's delegation opposed the bay cap
The vote was held earlier in the week

leftOut.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to limit judges' power to void rules nationwide
leftOut.summary:
The US Justice Department has asked the Supreme Court to restrict courts' power under the Administrative Procedure Act to set aside federal rules for everyone rather than only for the parties to a case, Reuters reported in an analysis. The appeal stems from a challenge by Texas medical providers to federal surprise-billing rules.

The administration argues relief should be limited to plaintiffs, while Republican-led states including Texas and Florida say the law is a key check on federal overreach, according to Reuters. The court is expected to decide early next year whether to hear the case.
keyFacts: The 5th Circuit voided parts of the billing rule nationwide in August
A 2025 ruling limited universal injunctions but not this issue
The piece is a Reuters analysis

leftOut.title: All accounted for after tanker strikes river cruise boat in New Orleans
leftOut.summary:
Everyone aboard the American Heritage river cruise boat was accounted for after a tanker struck it on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans on Friday, city officials said, according to ABC News in the US. Officials said nearly 200 people were aboard.

About 30 passengers and two crew who ended up in the water were taken to hospital with non-critical injuries, ABC News reported. Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said the tanker appeared to have lost steering. The National Transportation Safety Board sent investigators, and part of the river was closed.
keyFacts: The collision happened about 12:30pm local time
The tanker was the Atlantic Asphalt
The boat appeared to be docked when struck, CBS said

leftOut.title: Lambie says government should consider means testing childcare and EV subsidies
leftOut.summary:
Tasmanian senator Jacqui Lambie has said the federal government should consider means testing childcare subsidies and electric vehicle incentives, the ABC reported. She made the comments as debate continues over the budget position and spending on household support.

The government has defended its childcare reforms as giving families access to subsidised care, and has already moved to limit some tax benefits for electric vehicles from 2027. The Coalition has also questioned the cost of universal childcare. Senator Lambie's comments are a call for policy change rather than a decision, and the government has not indicated it will adopt her proposals.
keyFacts: Lambie raised means testing for childcare subsidies
She also raised means testing EV incentives
The government has not adopted the idea

leftOut.title: Man in critical condition after lightning strike at Ettalong Beach
leftOut.summary:
A man is in a critical condition after being struck by lightning at Ettalong Beach on the NSW Central Coast, the ABC reported. AAP reported the man was swimming when he was hit, and forecasters warned of further storm risk.

AAP described the event as "blue sky lightning", which can strike some distance from a storm. The man was taken to hospital, according to the ABC. Authorities advise people to leave beaches and water when thunder is heard. Further thunderstorms were forecast for parts of NSW and Queensland after storms earlier in the week cut power to tens of thousands of homes.
keyFacts: The man was struck at Ettalong Beach
He is in a critical condition
More storms were forecast

leftOut.title: Two bushwalkers rescued from Western Arthur Range in Tasmania
leftOut.summary:
Two bushwalkers have been rescued from the Western Arthur Range in Tasmania's south-west, the ABC reported. The range is a remote and rugged part of the Tasmanian Wilderness World Heritage Area.

The ABC reported the pair were rescued on Sunday. The circumstances that led to the rescue and the condition of the walkers were not detailed beyond the ABC's report. Tasmania Police regularly urge walkers in remote areas to carry a personal locator beacon, register their plans and check weather forecasts before setting out, as conditions in the south-west can change quickly.
keyFacts: Two walkers were rescued
The rescue was in the Western Arthur Range
The area is in Tasmania's south-west

leftOut.title: Philippines wins first Eurovision Asia song contest in Bangkok
leftOut.summary:
The Philippines has won the inaugural Eurovision Asia song contest, held in Bangkok, Thailand, the ABC reported. The event is an Asian spin-off of the long-running European music competition.

The ABC reported the contest debuted in Bangkok this weekend with entrants from countries across Asia and the Pacific. Australia has competed in the European contest since 2015. Organisers have presented the Asian contest as a way to bring the Eurovision format to new audiences in the region, and the ABC reported the debut event drew entrants from a range of countries.
keyFacts: The Philippines won
It was the first Eurovision Asia
The contest was held in Bangkok

leftOut.title: New York Democratic Socialists urge Ocasio-Cortez to run for US president
leftOut.summary:
New York members of the Democratic Socialists of America have urged Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to run for president, Al Jazeera reported. The call follows strong results for socialist candidates in New York in recent elections.

Ms Ocasio-Cortez has not announced any decision on a 2028 run. Speculation about her plans has been reported for weeks, with Jacobin reporting in October that the DSA was eyeing a campaign and the Daily Signal and Fox News reporting divisions within the group over an early endorsement. Other Democrats, including California Governor Gavin Newsom, have also said they are weighing presidential bids.
keyFacts: The call came from New York DSA members
Ocasio-Cortez has not announced a decision
The next presidential election is in 2028

leftOut.title: Hundreds of men march in Switzerland against violence against women
leftOut.summary:
Hundreds of men have marched in Switzerland to protest against violence against women, Al Jazeera reported. The march was organised to show men's opposition to gendered violence.

Al Jazeera reported the participants marched to call for an end to violence against women. The event comes ahead of the UN's International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November, when rallies are held in many countries. Organisers presented the march as a show of men's support for ending gendered violence.
keyFacts: Hundreds of men took part
The march was in Switzerland
It protested violence against women

leftOut.title: Francophone summit opens in Cambodia amid Rwanda–Congo rift
leftOut.summary:
The summit of La Francophonie, the international organisation of French-speaking countries, has opened in Cambodia, Al Jazeera reported. The meeting is taking place amid tension between member states Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Cambodia is hosting the 20th summit of the organisation. Al Jazeera reported the rift between Kigali and Kinshasa, which have long been at odds over armed groups in eastern Congo, overshadowed the opening. Cambodian outlets reported more than 20 leaders were expected. No major decisions had been announced at the opening session, according to the reports reviewed.

Cambodia is the host
Rwanda and Congo remain at odds

leftOut.title: Kangaroos withdraw centre from Rugby League World Cup final with illness
leftOut.summary:
Australia's Kangaroos have withdrawn a centre from Sunday's Rugby League World Cup final against New Zealand because of illness, AAP reported. The men's final is part of a double-header in which the Jillaroos also play New Zealand.

The player's late withdrawal forced a change to the Kangaroos' line-up, AAP reported. SBS reported both Australian sides face New Zealand in finals played on the same day, and the ABC ran live coverage of both matches. Australia has won the men's tournament more often than any other country.
keyFacts: The Kangaroos lost a centre to illness
Both finals are against New Zealand
The finals are a double-header

leftOut.title: Warner makes further comments on 2018 ball-tampering scandal
leftOut.summary:
Former Australian opener David Warner has made further comments about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal, AAP reported. The remarks follow claims this week by former teammate Usman Khawaja that the whole team knew of the plan, which captain Pat Cummins rejected.

AAP reported Mr Warner's latest comments added to the public dispute between former and current players over who knew about the use of sandpaper in Cape Town. Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation found three players responsible. The players involved served bans at the time, and Mr Warner has since retired from international cricket.
keyFacts: Warner commented again on the 2018 scandal
Khawaja says the whole team knew; Cummins rejects that
Cricket Australia's 2018 inquiry found three players responsible

leftOut.title: Government seeks gas reserve deal before final parliamentary weeks of 2026
leftOut.summary:
The federal government could still secure passage of its domestic gas reserve before parliament rises for the year, AAP reported, ahead of a Senate-only sitting starting Monday. The plan would require exporters to set aside up to 20 per cent of exports for local use.

Labor needs Coalition or Greens support. In a Senate inquiry report, the Coalition said it was open to the policy with changes, while Coalition senators Kerrynne Liddle and Susan McDonald said the current design would hurt domestic producers. Eight groups including the Australian Industry Group and the ACTU urged the Senate to pass it, AAP said.
keyFacts: Senate-only sitting begins Monday
Reserve would cover up to 20 per cent of exports
Coalition says it is open to the plan with changes

leftOut.title: RBA minutes due Tuesday after split vote on November rate rise
leftOut.summary:
Minutes of the Reserve Bank's November meeting are due on Tuesday, after three of nine board members voted against lifting the cash rate to 4.85 per cent on 3 November, AAP reported. It was the bank's fifth increase in a year and took the rate to an 18-year high.

September quarter wage figures are due on Wednesday, with economists expecting annual growth of 3.4 per cent, and October jobs data on Thursday, with unemployment tipped to stay at 4.7 per cent, according to AAP. NAB economist Josh Copeland said he expected employment growth above 20,000.
keyFacts: Three of nine RBA board members opposed the November rise
Cash rate is 4.85 per cent, an 18-year high
Wages data due Wednesday and jobs data Thursday

leftOut.title: Lambie says Hanson has not apologised personally over One Nation cartoon
leftOut.summary:
Tasmanian senator Jacqui Lambie said on ABC's Insiders on Sunday that One Nation leader Pauline Hanson had not apologised to her directly over an October online cartoon that mocked her health, AAP reported. The video has since been removed from One Nation's YouTube page.

Senator Lambie said she had no relationship with Senator Hanson and that One Nation's rise in polls reflected financial strain on voters, according to AAP. She urged upper house members to moderate the tone of debate as parliament returns on Monday for a Senate-only sitting week. One Nation had earlier asked the video's creator to amend it.
keyFacts: Lambie spoke on ABC's Insiders on Sunday
Cartoon removed from One Nation's YouTube page
Senate sits from Monday

leftOut.title: Zelenskiy says Russia launched more than 2,300 drones at Ukraine in a week
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Sunday that Russia launched more than 2,300 attack drones, 1,590 guided bombs and 15 missiles at Ukraine over the past week, hitting energy and rail infrastructure, Kyiv Post reported. At least 16 people were injured.

Mr Zelenskiy repeated that speed limits on Starshield satellite terminals stop Ukrainian interceptor drones from chasing jet-powered Shahed drones, and said he had told officials to work with the US government and SpaceX to restore full service, according to Kyiv Post. US senators Jeanne Shaheen and Chris Coons have written to SpaceX seeking compliance by 30 November.
keyFacts: Over 2,300 drones, 1,590 guided bombs and 15 missiles in a week, Zelenskiy says
At least 16 people injured
Zelenskiy again raised Starshield speed limits

leftOut.title: Independent MP Helen Haines discharged from hospital after Wangaratta attack
leftOut.summary:
Independent federal MP Helen Haines has been discharged from The Alfred hospital in Melbourne, ABC News reported on Monday. Dr Haines lost both legs after being struck by a car outside her Wangaratta electorate office on 19 October.

Politicians from across parliament welcomed the news, according to the ABC's live coverage. A 43-year-old man, Brendan Nugent, has been charged over the incident, the ABC reported. The charges have not been tested in court. Details of Dr Haines's return to parliamentary duties were not reported in the coverage reviewed.

She lost both legs after being hit by a car on 19 October
A 43-year-old man has been charged

leftOut.title: Ecuadorian fishers who survived US drone strike plan lawsuit against US government
leftOut.summary:
Sixteen Ecuadorian fishers who say they survived a US military drone strike on their boat in March are suing the US government, Common Dreams reported. They are represented by lawyer Dan Kovalik in the US District Court for the Western District of Pennsylvania, according to the report.

The fishers allege the strike on the vessel La Negra Francesca Duarte II was unlawful and that they were later detained in El Salvador, and seek unspecified damages, Common Dreams said. It cited The Guardian as reporting the filing was due on Monday US time. The US government's response was not reported, and the filing had not been confirmed.
keyFacts: 16 fishers say a US drone strike sank their boat in March
Suit to be lodged in the Western District of Pennsylvania
Filing had not been confirmed at the time of reporting

leftOut.title: Van Hollen says he won't back funding for Iran war ahead of December deadline
leftOut.summary:
US Democratic senator Chris Van Hollen said he would not vote for any spending bill that funds the war with Iran, Jewish Insider reported, ahead of a 11 December government funding deadline. He said that if President Donald Trump was prepared to shut down the government to continue the war, that would be the president's decision.

Some other Senate Democrats have taken similar positions, according to Jewish Insider. The White House's response to his remarks was not reported. The remarks restate a position Mr Van Hollen first set out earlier in November, and no vote has been scheduled on the funding bills.
keyFacts: Van Hollen says he won't fund the Iran war
US government funding expires on 11 December
No vote on the bills has been scheduled

leftOut.title: India warns Bay of Bengal system could become severe cyclone by 17 November
leftOut.summary:
The India Meteorological Department said a depression over the Bay of Bengal was likely to strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm by 17 November and move towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, Business Today reported. A landfall point had not been forecast.

Odisha's disaster management minister Suresh Pujari put all districts on alert, according to the report, after two earlier cyclones in recent weeks. Fishermen were told to return to shore by 16 November, and rain is expected on 18 and 19 November. No damage or casualties had been reported, as the storm had not yet formed.
keyFacts: IMD expects a severe cyclonic storm by 17 November
Odisha placed all districts on alert
Fishermen told to return to shore

leftOut.title: Iran rejects German demand to halt uranium enrichment
leftOut.summary:
Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected a German call for Tehran to stop enriching uranium, citing Iran's rights under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, the Associated Press reported. He also criticised the International Atomic Energy Agency over speculation about a new facility near Isfahan.

Mr Baghaei said the IAEA had lost access during the war with the US and Israel, and that Iran would respond to any attack, according to AP. Germany has said Iran must halt enrichment to ease tensions. The comments repeat Iran's long-stated position on enrichment, and no new nuclear talks were announced.
keyFacts: Iran rejects Germany's call to halt enrichment
Spokesman cites Iran's rights under the NPT
Criticised IAEA over Isfahan speculation
